a.text: 'Salt is sacred. It is within the tides, within our tears.'

steps.text: He strains his eyes in the dark waters, searching the lake bed for the faint glint of metal.
He slowly paddles forward, inch by inch, fingers outstretched in the silt, but all they find are strands of waterweeds.
The frigid waters flow past his skin and hair. Confusion sets in. He does not know how he will find that golden coin.

a.text: 'Don't look with your eyes. Let the water's flow tell you where to go.'

steps.text: A voice from ashore cuts through the water. He cannot see the person's face clearly, but that gentle, friendly tone sounds reassuring.
And so he closes his eyes, feeling the water rush past him, and painting an image of the lake bed in his mind's eye.
There. A solid metal disc, embossed with a complex design, resting atop some wafting weeds.
He strokes its face before grasping it in his hand. He swims away, the stranger's face getting ever clearer as he gets closer to shore.

a.text: 'Did you find the coin, my boy?'

steps.text: He unfurls his fingers, the gold coin resting on his palm. The circle on its face is bisected by a straight line. Somehow it resembles some distant horizon, one he has yet to reach.

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: Urgh...

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: What's that smell... Finny... Salty...

steps.name: Strange Creature
steps.text: Mm... hmph...

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: *Sigh*...

steps.name: Strange Creature
steps.text: (Sticks out tongue) Bleh...

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: Don't lick my face, little guy, or I'll hit you.

steps.name: Strange Creature
steps.text: Mmph...

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: Forget it. I won't have to deal with you much longer.

steps.name: Coarse Male Voice
steps.text: Hey, chaval, your food. Eat up quick! Boss wants to see you!

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: She won't be seeing me today.
Isidro pulls down the canvas hammock hung up in the room, wrapping it around the hard bread and half-full canister of water on the tray.
He then kicks open the chest by his side, revealing a tunnel below it.
He had been digging away at it for a full week.
The strange-looking animal crawls up and nips onto his pants. Isidro watches its saliva soak into the fabric and sighs.

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: I'm definitely not coming back here.

steps.name: Fiery Woman
steps.text: (Whistle) Javier, can I get that blade I left here last month?

steps.name: Fiery Woman
steps.text: Javier!

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: Eh? Oh... Sorry, Teach, wasn't listening. You here for the blade?

steps.name: Teach
steps.text: What else? Not your sweat-stained pecs, I'll tell you that much.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: You all need to stop it with the jokes, Teach.

steps.name: Teach
steps.text: Oh, don't be like that. Seeing you sharpening knives in the early morn is pretty much part of the landscape by now.

steps.name: Teach
steps.text: Look, you've drawn in a crowd... Though I don't think they're here to get their knives polished.

steps.name: Spectating Man
steps.text: (Leers) Hey there, Javier!

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: What a pain in the— Here. Your blade.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: We don't have much metal left for repairs, so I used other things to fix it up. You'll have to make do with it for a while.

steps.name: Teach
steps.text: Shell and bone? You're a real dab hand.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: Wanna test it?

steps.name: Teach
steps.text: Got anything tough I can chop up?

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: I did have a hunk of dry bread... but I just gave it to the kid locked in the shack.

steps.name: Teach
steps.text: Waste of a perfectly good loaf.
Hey, hey, move it already! Don't you lot have anything better to do in the morning? Stop blocking the damn way!

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: Rus?

steps.name: Teach
steps.text: Oh, it's you. And here I was, thinking it was the harsh glare of dawn in my eyes.

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: I don't have time for you and your nonsense. Quick, Javier, let's head inside and talk!

steps.name: Teach
steps.text: Sounds like it's not for my ears. I'll be off then, Javier.

steps.name: Spectating Man
steps.text: Seems like the fun has ended... See you tomorrow, Javier!

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: (Quietly) Hmph...

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: You need to talk to Juana. She's gone mad! She's going to send us all to our deaths, and you're the only one in her crew who can keep a cool head!

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: And how is that new?

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: Over all these years, every single one of her decisions looked crazy at first, but turned out to be exactly what we needed, right?

spans.text: of her decisions looked crazy at first, but turned out to be exactly what we needed, right?

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: Getting in touch with that caravan a decade ago was a huge gamble too, but here we are, making a good living selling antiques we dig out of the salt flat.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: Nobody took her side back then. Everyone was too scared of those money-grubbing merchants leaking the location of our fleet to the Inquisition.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: But Juana got them to see what the real value of the deal was, and made them an offer they couldn't refuse.

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: This is different, Javier. Totally different.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: Doesn't matter, Rus. She's our boss, and I'd say she's earned our trust.

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: She wants us to go back out to sea. You really going to back her on this? You really think this is a way forward?

spans.text: She wants us to go back out to sea. You really going to back her on this? You
think this is a way forward?

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: 'Cause it's not. We're all just gonna end up in a watery grave.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: Show a little faith. She found the compass, and a caster to fix it up. Everything's going to plan, no?

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: Even if you don't give a damn what happens outside your kitchen, you must've noticed the finshit you've been getting to cook with lately, yeah?

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: Look, here are the bills for the wood she's been buying up. All to fix those rotten old ships, all to head back out to that sea of hers.

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: You know how expensive wood is. All that coin could've made our lives much cozier. You wouldn't be slaving away every day pickling saltfin livers for garum, I can say that much.

spans.text: how expensive wood is. All that coin could've made our lives much cozier. You wouldn't be slaving away every day pickling saltfin livers for garum, I can say that much.

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: Just go talk to her, afore she's done too much damage.

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: Been hearing some real nasty talk around town. Folks're getting restless.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: Fine, I'll have a chat with her.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: But don't forget, Rus. Without that 'loca' Juana, our grandparents, our parents, us...

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: None of us would've been able to live out here in the Salt Flat.

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: Strange...

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: Where did that cook go? The one always sitting outside.

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: Mierda...

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: Are they trying to take me back?
A man turns the corner, aggression apparent in his footsteps. Isidro quickly hides himself in a shadowy corner.
But the man walks right by him, swearing up a storm as he goes.

steps.name: Aggressive Man
steps.text: Idiots! You blasted idiots!

steps.name: Aggressive Man
steps.text: Just you wait and see, that puta's going to get us all killed!

steps.name: Teach
steps.text: Clear your head, Cesc. You've been eating that girl's herbs on the sly again.

steps.name: Cesc
steps.text: My head's clear as day, it's yours I'm worried about!

steps.name: Cesc
steps.text: I can't be the only one with a problem with how she's leading us, can I?

steps.name: Cesc
steps.text: You're all just too yellow to say it. Cowards, the lot of you!

steps.name: Teach
steps.text: Vete a la mierda. If you're going to spew shit, do it at home.

steps.name: Cesc
steps.text: But am I wrong, Teach?!

steps.name: Cesc
steps.text: Don't tell me you trust that loca too?!

steps.name: Cesc
steps.text: Have you been taken in by her saltdamned lies too, like Javier?!

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: Cesc...

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: Hey, cool it! He's just a little upset!

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: Say that again.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: Say. That. Again.

steps.name: Cesc
steps.text: You know I'm right, Javier.

steps.name: Cesc
steps.text: All those years of licking her boots. Shouting 'aye aye, Captain!' at all her shit.

steps.name: Cesc
steps.text: We all know you're a loyal beckbeast.

steps.name: Cesc
steps.text: So put down that knife of yours and go crying to Mamá like always.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: You—!
Javier grabs Cesc by the collar and lifts him up, slamming his back into the wall.
Javier's face is calm, but the fire in his eyes burns bright, nearly bright enough to sear holes into the target of his ire.

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: Are they going to start a fight...?

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: If they do, I may as well make a break for it.

steps.name: Cesc
steps.text: Urk...

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: Don't you ever spew that sort of finshit again. Not even in your sleep.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: You hear me, Cesc?
Cesc can barely breathe as Javier presses into his neck. Nobody dares approach the two, only silently passing them with their heads lowered.
The people in the sheds lining the street shut their windows tight one after the other. In a flash, the street is empty.

steps.name: Cesc
steps.text: Ugh...

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: Let him go, Javier! He's learned his lesson!

steps.name: Teach
steps.text: (Whispers) Not here, Javier...

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: ANSWER ME!

steps.name: Cesc
steps.text: (Nods furiously)

steps.name: Cesc
steps.text: *cough*... *cough* *cough* *cough*—!

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: Now run along home, chaval. Remember what you learned today. Remember it well.

steps.name: Teach
steps.text: *Sigh* The hell was that, Javier? You've never been that reckless.

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: Reckless? No. He was just making it clear to everyone where he stands.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: Rus, I...

steps.name: Teach
steps.text: Relax, just bring him a little something tonight. He'll accept your apology.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: Yeah. Thanks, Teach.
Javier watches the woman walk away as he stands in the middle of the street.
A stray headscarf lies at his feet, having fallen off Cesc's head as he ran.
Javier picks it up, pats off the dust, and walks back to his shed, closing the door lightly behind him.

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: Good, everyone's gone.

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: I was afraid I'd have to wait for them all to take an afternoon siesta.

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: Tch...

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: Why did I even try escaping at night last time? That's when these guys are most active.

spans.text: escaping at night last time? That's when these guys are most active.

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: (There. That's my way out. Just need to head down.)

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: (Only two guards. Gotta knock them out.)

steps.name: Inattentive Guard
steps.text: Ahem...

steps.name: Inattentive Guard
steps.text: Say, Anna... Ever thought about going someplace else?

steps.name: Inattentive Guard
steps.text: I kept some of those old coins we've been digging up. File off the king's face, and you can barely tell the difference from the new ones!

steps.name: Inattentive Guard
steps.text: We could leave the Flat behind. Go to Rim Billiton, Columbia... Anywhere you'd like.

steps.name: Diligent Guard
steps.text: No, José. I was born and raised here. Never even thought of leaving.

steps.name: Inattentive Guard
steps.text: You really want to stay and follow the boss out to sea?

steps.name: Diligent Guard
steps.text: She's the boss.

steps.name: Inattentive Guard
steps.text: The sea'll swallow you up...

steps.name: Diligent Guard
steps.text: I ain't afraid. She promised us.

steps.name: Inattentive Guard
steps.text: Well, what scares me is that that promise might turn out to be a fleeting dream.

spans.text: is that that promise might turn out to be a fleeting dream.

steps.name: Diligent Guard
steps.text: If you're that scared, then go. I ain't gonna stop you.

steps.name: Inattentive Guard
steps.text: ...I was kinda hoping you would.

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: (Are they done yet?)

steps.name: Inattentive Guard
steps.text: If you don't wanna leave with me, then at least...

steps.name: Diligent Guard
steps.text: At least what?

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: (Can't this guy take a hint?)

steps.name: Inattentive Guard
steps.text: Could you, uh, give me a...

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: (Stop mumbling and spit it out alr—)

steps.name: Diligent Guard
steps.text: Stop mumbling and spit it out already!
Unable to bear watching the man stumble over his words any longer, the woman knocks him flat before sandwiching his face between her hands, kissing him hard.
Isidro furrows his brows before looking away politely.

steps.name: Inattentive Guard
steps.text: Mmmf... Anna...

steps.name: Diligent Guard
steps.text: Oh, just shut it!

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: (At least they didn't notice me.)

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: Phew...

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: Need to run faster... If I'm not out of here before dark...

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: Based on the last few times, I'm definitely going to be—
A giant helm wheel rolls past his face before coming to a halt, stopping just short of crushing his feet.
You shouldn't keep a lady waiting, you know.
Now be a good boy and come back with me.

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: You shouldn't be here.
Still not given up after all these attempts? We might not have enough spare medicine to patch you up if you end up wounded again, you know.

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: How did you know I was gone, Señora Juana?

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: I made sure nobody was following me.

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: It's my job to be aware of what's happening in my fleet. You can't hide from my little eyes and ears.

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: Besides, did no one ever teach you not to ask a lady a question she'd rather not answer?
The young man does not reply, silently thinking of the sword that had been faithfully at his side for years. If he still had it, perhaps it would even the odds.
But it had shattered. Just like the freedom currently within arm's reach, it had died in these salt flats, snapped in two.
Isidro clenches his fist, grits his teeth, and grabs onto whatever is left of his things.
The lady lightly draws her sword, her stance relaxed.

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: Out of my way!

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: Ngh—
After a few sword strokes, the unarmed man falls defeated, face in the salty sand. He could not protect even the last of his belongings.
As Juana ties him up and heaves him over her shoulder, he feels something in his heart silently shatter.

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: Ah, youth. Never knowing when to give up. No matter how many times you're beaten down, you're already dreaming of the next attempt.

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: If you're that desperate to leave, then fix that compass for me.

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: How many times I have to say it? Only an alchemist can fix it, and I'm no alchemist!

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: Oh? Then care to explain where that gold coin of yours came from?

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: ...I stole it.

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: You are a terrible liar, joven.

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: On its face is a mark only a few know of: the mark of the long-lost school of alchemy. The knowledge they passed down helped countless fleets find treasure in the seas.

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: But after the Profound Silence, their disciples were imprisoned, and their works destroyed.

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: So tell me, why are you holding onto that coin, despite all that happened to them?

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: I don't know anything about any of that.

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: Oh, what a stubborn young man. How about we change the question, then?

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: How did you dig that tunnel of yours?

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: ...The bread you gave me was really hard.

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: What a clever boy.

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: My oh my, I really must thank you!

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: You've worked so hard keeping watch over him. Why, if you hadn't informed me right away, he might have actually gotten away.

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: Yes, I know, he's not the best-behaved prisoner, but that's why we have you, isn't it?

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: You really are our cleverest, sharpest-witted, most amazing little...

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: Nene.

steps.name: Nene
steps.text: Mm-ph!

steps.name: Nene
steps.text: (Spins excitedly)

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: Don't get too excited now. There are still many difficult duties ahead of you, and you mustn't take them lightly.

steps.name: Nene
steps.text: (Quickly falls flat on the ground)

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: I have faith in you, of course. Alright, off you go now. Don't let that boy learn who you are.

steps.name: Nene
steps.text: Mmph!

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: Come in, Javi.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: Pardon me, Señora Juana. I hope I'm not interrupting your time with Nene.

steps.name: Nene
steps.text: Mmph...

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: Don't give me that look. I've got a little something for you too.

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: My, what a fine little ball of bone... Did you carve it?

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: Sí. Out of bone shards that broke off some of our older weapons. Else they'd have gone to waste.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: I wanted to give it to Rus as an apology, but he won't open his door for me.

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: Oh... I did hear about that. You shouldn't be so hasty, Javier. As our fleet's bosun, Rus has every right to question my plan to go out to sea.

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: And you attacking one of his men right in front of him can be seen as a rather harsh warning.

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: Considering your recent promotion to main chef, best keep a low profile. Some things are better left unsaid.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: I think he's the one who needed that advice.

spans.text: the one who needed that advice.

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: Just let him be, Javi. I don't pay it any mind, so why should you?

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: Because I know our boss isn't a madwoman playing around with other people's lives.

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: Well, aren't you sweet?

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: If we do get that compass fixed, can it really tell us how to avoid the sea monsters and find what we need?

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: Of course. I would never lie to you, Javi.

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: The Salt Flat won't be able to support us for generations to come. While the sea is a nigh inexhaustible font of resources.

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: Now that we have both the 'compass' and an alchemist to fix it, this is a chance for us to turn our lives around. We can't afford to miss it.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: But aside from you, none of us have even seen the sea, or experienced that age of gold and plenty.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: I've been living in the Flat for as long as I can remember, but the old cook said that only a century ago, this was fertile soil.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: What if that bountiful sea of yours has already become just as barren as the Flat after the Profound Silence?

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: And this magic compass of yours... can't guide us back to the past.

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: 'The tides will wash away my footprints, and the wind will scrub away the foam from the waves.'

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: 'But the sea and the shore will stand, forevermore.'

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: What...?

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: Just an old poem, Javi. Unlike the land, the sea is tenacious. Though it may be infested with strangely fleshed beasts, it is still abundant with precious lifelines, waiting for us to find them.

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: It was once ours, and it can be ours once again.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: I want to believe you, I do.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: But these rumors... You have to prove yourself in front of everyone, show them you're not talking nonsense.

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: I will.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: Oh, right. I did as you asked and went by the shed. There really is a hole in there. I'll fill it up tonight.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: What should we do about the boy? He can't stay there anymore.

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: Don't worry, I've already found a place for him.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: But where? If you mean my place, then no.

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: Don't you worry your little head over it. You'll see on your way home.

steps.name: Angry Man
steps.text: Damned little brat, this peg-leg you sold me is pure garbage! Two days and it's already split in twain!

steps.name: Conniving Vendor
steps.text: Eh, it just needs a bit of spit, polish, and glue and it'll be good as new.

steps.name: Angry Man
steps.text: You sack of finshit, how about I rip your leg off and use that instead?!

spans.text: You sack of finshit, how about I rip
leg off and use that instead?!

steps.name: Conniving Vendor
steps.text: H-Hey, settle down now! I'll take the leg back, no need to get violent!

steps.name: Conniving Vendor
steps.text: I-I-I've got a knife! Don't come any closer!

steps.name: Angry Man
steps.text: Javier! Right on time! Help me catch the little wench!

steps.name: Conniving Vendor
steps.text: Out of my way, idiot!

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: Tch... Troublemaker.

steps.name: Conniving Vendor
steps.text: Ow! That hurts!

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: Give him back his money.

steps.name: Conniving Vendor
steps.text: Let me go! I'll tell Juana you've been bullying me!

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: Use your head, chica. This isn't somewhere you can run your mouth. We're not like those cowards in other towns.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: If you mess with us, we won't bother locking you up or putting you on trial. Left hand or right hand? Choose the one you want to keep.

steps.name: Conniving Vendor
steps.text: H-How dare you! If it weren't for me, your boss would never have gotten ahold of that compass!

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: Care to try your luck?

steps.name: Conniving Vendor
steps.text: Err... Fine, I'll return the money! But you gotta give me back that peg-leg!

steps.name: Angry Man
steps.text: Not on my life. If it's stuck to my leg, it's mine.

steps.name: Conniving Vendor
steps.text: Y-You're no better than a pack of bandits!

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: I'm glad you've finally come to an accurate assessment of us, señorita.

steps.name: Conniving Vendor
steps.text: Haha... Slip of the tongue is all... Here, the money. And, uh, adios.

steps.name: Angry Man
steps.text: What was the boss thinking, letting a dastardly little girl like that aboard our crew?

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: She's got her reasons.

steps.name: Angry Man
steps.text: I heard that kid ran off again. Why not just break his legs and be done with it?

steps.name: Angry Man
steps.text: And now she's gone and strung him up here, ordering us not to touch a hair on his head. Seeing that grumpy face of his pisses me right off. You don't know how much I wanna give it a good punch.

steps.name: Angry Man
steps.text: Hey, don't go, Javier! I was just thinking out loud!

steps.name: Angry Man
steps.text: Hey!

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: You've been running around all day. Want some water?

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: Cloudbeast got your tongue?

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: I won't surrender to you lot.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: If that's how you want it, chaval.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: Just here to give you the bad news. I'm afraid you're going to be out here like this all night.

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: ...Whatever. I don't care.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: Good to hear.
The dawn light falls upon the coin, and a stray ray reflects onto Isidro's eyelid, causing him to blink. The light wanders, and the circular marking on the coin begins to ripple.
He begins to feel discomfort and hands the coin to the man ashore, though the man is in no hurry to receive it. Instead, he grabs onto Isidro's legs and lifts him up by the feet.
The boy struggles, and the man ashore begins to speak:

a.text: 'If you have nowhere to go, my young friend, you can come with me.'
'They call me Aulus, and you have my thanks for finding my coin.'

steps.text: The rays of the setting sun seep through the cracks of the salt ship's frame, shining onto Isidro's eyelid. He blinks in discomfort.
People walk by, and none can resist snickering at him as they pass.
He feels a little dizzy. The faint laughter causes his cheeks to flush, though it might just be an effect of being hung upside down.
Out here in the Salt Flat, simple tents and ramshackle shacks are put up one after the other.
Enormous salt ships are berthed on either side of the road, like a herd of slumbering seabeasts.
Upon their masts hang great sacks for gathering rainwater, flapping in the wind as they await clouds to pass overhead.
Upon the road, people walk shoulder to shoulder, laughing and squabbling, until all of a sudden a quarrel breaks out, which soon escalates into a chaotic all-out brawl.
And in the quieter corners, some are pulling their lovers in close for an intimate kiss.

steps.name: Conniving Vendor
steps.text: These guys really are a bunch of barbarians.

steps.name: Conniving Vendor
